requested.title: What If You Could Pause Time for 10 Seconds a Day?
requested.description:
You wake up and you can stop the world. Ten seconds, once a day. What would you spend them on?

The first days, day twelve, the catch, and forty years lived ten seconds at a time.

What would you do with your ten seconds? Tell us in the comments. The best what-ifs become videos.

Chapters
0:00 Ten seconds
0:23 The rules
0:53 The first days
1:53 Day twelve
2:43 The catch
3:49 The long run
4:52 The twist

The power is made up. The numbers are real:
- A phone falls a metre in about 0.45 seconds: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, 2.7 Falling Objects
  https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/2-7-falling-objects
- At a normal walking pace, ten seconds covers about 10 to 14 metres: Bohannon and Andrews (2011)
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21820535/
- The clock that seems to stop when you glance at it is called chronostasis: Yarrow et al., Nature (2001)
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11713528/
- A car at 48 km/h needs about 23 metres to stop: The Highway Code, typical stopping distances
  https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/65f97642aa9b760011fbda4e/the-highway-code-stopping-distances.pdf

Narrated with an AI voice. Animated in code. Also available with a Hindi audio track.
